The Touristenfahrten layout, a true test of endurance. This isn't just a race; it's a battle against the Nordschleife itself.

historicalReferences: Think of Bernd Rosemeyer in the Auto Union, dominating the pre-war era. The ghosts of giants haunt these hallowed grounds.
Niki Lauda's fiery crash in 1976 forever changed the Nürburgring, a stark reminder of the dangers inherent in this sport.
The legendary battles between Jackie Stewart and the Nordschleife, earning him the moniker 'The Green Hell', echo through the ages.
Stefan Bellof's incredible lap record in 1983, a benchmark that stood for decades, is a testament to the track's demanding nature.
The FIA GT Championship races of the late 90s and early 2000s provided some incredible racing action on this very circuit.
The 24 Hours Nürburgring, a grueling endurance test, has produced countless dramatic moments and unforgettable victories on this layout.
Michael Schumacher's mastery of the Nordschleife is legendary. His precision and commitment were unparalleled.
Many manufacturers use this circuit to test the limits of their cars, a proving ground for performance and reliability.
The early days of Grand Prix racing at the Nürburgring were a spectacle of speed and bravery, setting the stage for the circuit's iconic status.
The sheer length of the track has always been a factor, demanding both driver skill and mechanical endurance, leading to both triumphs and heartbreak.
cornerCallouts: Here they come into Hatzenbach, a tricky chicane that demands precision and courage.
Through the Schwedenkreuz, one of the fastest and most daunting sections of the entire circuit.
Now approaching Aremberg, a deceptively simple corner that can easily catch drivers out.
The cars dive into Fuchsröhre, a rollercoaster ride of compression and blind crests.
It's the Karussell, the infamous banked corner, a real test of the car's suspension and the driver's nerve.
Down the long Dottinger Hohe straight, a chance to stretch the legs and gain valuable time.
Navigating the tricky Pflanzgarten jumps, where getting it wrong can have serious consequences.
And finally, the run to the finish line after negotiating Galgenkopf. What a lap!
strategyPoints: Tire management is absolutely crucial on this 20.832km layout. One wrong move and the rubber will be gone before you reach the halfway point.
The pit window is long here, around 45 seconds. Teams need to factor that into their calculations.
Fuel load is a major consideration. Too much fuel and you're carrying unnecessary weight; too little and you're gambling on a late safety car.
With such a long lap, a safety car can completely change the complexion of the race. Timing is everything.
The undulating nature of the track puts immense strain on the brakes. Expect to see some brake fade towards the end of the stint.
Traffic management is key. Overtaking opportunities are limited, so getting a clean run is vital.
The Touristenfahrten layout's length means teams will be constantly monitoring tire degradation and making adjustments on the fly.
A crucial strategic decision: when to switch to the harder compound tires to ensure a strong finish on this unforgiving circuit.
weatherCommentary: The Eifel mountains are notorious for unpredictable weather. Rain can sweep in at any moment, turning the track into an ice rink.
Fog can be a major issue at the Nürburgring, especially in the early morning. Visibility can be severely reduced.
The microclimates around the circuit are incredible. It can be raining in one section and dry in another.
The wind can also play a significant role, affecting the car's stability, particularly through the high-speed sections.
That classic Eifel mist is beginning to roll in, making conditions even more treacherous on this already challenging circuit.
